question:
Classify each of the following statements as True or False:
(a) Electropositivity of an element is inversely proportional to its electronegativity.
(b) Sigma bond can be formed by lateral overlap of two p-orbitals.
(c) A reaction occurring in a vacuum flask is an example of an isolated system.
(d) Metals have sonorous property.
(e) There are no intermolecular forces of attraction between real gas molecules.
How many moles of $\text{Br}_2$ are there in $15.98\text{ g}$ of $\text{Br}_2$?
How many moles of $\text{KOH}$ are there in $1\text{ dm}^3$ of its $3\text{ mole dm}^{-3}$ aqueous solution?
How many atoms are there in two moles of cobalt?
How many atoms are there in $0.1\text{ mole}$ of silicon?
What is the mass of $6.023 \times 10^{23}$ molecules of fluorine?

A $35.5\text{ g}$ of a gaseous compound, $\text{Y}_2\text{O}_5$ occupies a volume of $5.60\text{ dm}^3$ at standard temperature and pressure. Calculate the relative molar mass of (a) $\text{Y}_2\text{O}_5$; (b) $\text{Y}$.

Consider the elements: $\text{Na}$, $\text{Si}$, $\text{Mg}$, $\text{P}$, $\text{S}$, $\text{Ar}$, $\text{B}$, $\text{Cl}$. Which of these elements:
(a) forms a hydride with empirical formula, $\text{XH}_3$?
(b) exists as a diatomic molecule at room temperature?
(c) is monoatomic at room temperature?
(d) is the most electropositive?
(e) has semiconducting property?
What are isotopes?
Why are isotopes chemically indistinguishable?
Give three (3) physical properties that can be used to differentiate between isotopes of an element.
List five (5) characteristic properties of s-block elements.
What is the normal boiling point of a substance?
Is it possible for water to boil at a temperature higher than its boiling point? Justify your answer with suitable reason(s).

You are given a mixture of three white crystalline substances P, Q and R. P sublimes but Q and R are not influenced by heat. All the substances are soluble in water. In addition, R is also soluble in methanol. Outline a method of separation to obtain pure samples of P, Q and R.
Explain hybridisation of atomic orbitals. (2 marks)
Explain three important types of hybridisation involving valence electrons in $s$- and $p$-orbitals. (18 marks)
State Fajan's rule and explain how it can be used to predict solubility of a compound. (5 marks)
Explain solubility product of a sparingly soluble salt. (3 marks)
Give two limitations of the concept of solubility product. (2 marks)
State 4 applications of the concept of solubility product. (4 marks)
What are transition metals? (2 marks)
Write the electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}$, $\text{Fe(II)}$, and $\text{Fe(III)}$ and show their electron-in-box notations. (6 marks)
In which of the oxidation states in c(i) would you expect the iron to be the most stable? Suggest suitable explanation for your answer. (3 marks)
Give the names of any two neutral ligands. (2 marks)
Draw a complete labelled Born-Haber cycle for the formation of sodium chloride. (6 marks)

Calculate the lattice energy of sodium chloride from the following data: (6 marks)
Standard heat of sublimation, $\Delta H_s$ of metallic sodium $= +108\text{ kJmol}^{-1}$,
Standard enthalpy of formation, $\Delta H_f$ of sodium chloride $= -411\text{ kJmol}^{-1}$,
Standard enthalpy of dissociation, $\Delta H_d$ of chlorine $= +242\text{ kJmol}^{-1}$,
Ionisation energy, $I$ of sodium $= +500\text{ kJmol}^{-1}$,
Electron affinity of chlorine atoms $= -364\text{ kJmol}^{-1}$.

The values of the lattice energies of potassium halides are:
| Compound | $\text{KF}$ | $\text{KCl}$ | $\text{KI}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lattice energy $(\text{kJ mol}^{-1})$ | $-813$ | $-710$ | $-643$ |
Explain the trend of the above values. (4 marks)
State three applications of bond energy. (3 marks)
Both carbon and silicon belong to group 14 of the periodic table, at room temperature silicon(IV) oxide is a giant solid but carbon(IV) oxide is a gas. (6 marks)
Lithium chloride is more soluble in ethoxyethane than sodium chloride. (4 marks)
Iodine forms compounds with oxidation number of $+7$ but fluorine can only form univalent compounds. (5 marks)
Nitrogen is markedly different from other members of the group 15 of the periodic table. (5 marks)
The odour of hydrogen sulphide gas is perceived when sodium hydrogen sulphide is dissolved in water. (5 marks)
Outline Dalton and Thompson theories/models of atom. (6 marks)
State three (3) limitations inherent in each of the models/theories in (a) above. (6 marks)

A $0.6\text{ mole}$ of copper(II) sulphide is treated with $1.40\text{ mole}$ of trioxonitrate(V) acid according to the equation:
$$3\text{CuS}_{(s)} + 8\text{HNO}_{3(aq)} \longrightarrow 3\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2{}_{(aq)} + 3\text{S}_{(s)} + 2\text{NO}_{(g)} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}_{(l)}$$
How many moles of copper(II) nitrate could be formed? (5 marks)
What is the limiting reagent in the reaction? (1 mark)
Calculate the number of moles of excess reagent left at the end of the reaction. (3 marks)
Cite one significance of actual yield in chemical manufacturing industries. (1 mark)
Give three (3) reasons why actual yield is normally less than calculated yield in the synthesis of compounds. (3 marks)
